children: The Thanksgiving holiday week was relatively quiet for EV makers, but

(TSLA) added more Cybercabs to its Texas roster in one day this week, lifting the total above 1,000. Rival Lucid (LCID) began fully driverless Gravity testing with Nuro and Uber (UBER), and U.S.-listed Chinese makers reported earnings and expansion plans.
Tesla Scales Cybercab Fleet And Dallas Service
Texas Department of Motor Vehicles data now lists 1,107 Cybercabs, bringing the state’s total robotaxi vehicles to 1,841, with roughly 60% Cybercabs and the remainder Model Ys.

Cybercabs, Tesla’s dedicated robotaxi offering with two seats and no steering wheels or pedals, operate in Austin and Dallas. The company launched services in Dallas last week after months of operating it purely in Austin.
Lucid, Nuro And Uber Start Driverless Bay Area Testing

Rival Lucid Motors, meanwhile, is moving towards the robotaxi market itself. Nuro, Lucid and Uber began fully driverless public-road testing of Lucid Gravity robotaxis in Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos and Sunnyvale this week. Employee rides are next, the company said.

The commercial launch, earlier aimed at late 2026, is now expected in the first quarter of 2027 in the Bay Area, with Houston later. Uber has committed to buying at least 35,000 Lucid vehicles fitted with the Nuro Driver technology for its own fleet.
Analyst Names Rivian A Top Pick
On Rivian (RIVN), Seaport Research initiated coverage with a 'Buy' rating and $18 target, highlighting the R2’s volume potential and autonomy options and terming it its top EV pick.

“Smart design choices (traditional SUV shape), RIVN’s strong software and tech leadership, expanding brand awareness and strong backlog will support meaningful delivery upside in 2027,” the firm said about the R2, as reported by EV.com.

The R2 is Rivian’s latest offering, priced lower than its other models. The company started deliveries of the vehicle in June with its higher-end variant, and hopes to add cheaper variants through next year. The lowest-priced variant is expected to be priced around $45,000, close to Tesla’s bestselling Model Y. The company expects the vehicle will scale volumes and drive it towards profitability.
Chinese EV Maker Updates

Chinese EV maker Li Auto (LI), meanwhile, reported third-quarter revenue of RMB 28.8 billion ($4.32 billion), up 5.4% year over year, on 99,964 deliveries. The company’s net loss narrowed to about RMB 310 million, gross margin recovered to 16.7%, and free cash flow turned positive at RMB 1.96 billion. Fourth-quarter guidance is 110,000–115,000 deliveries, compared to the 109,194 vehicles it actually delivered in Q4 2025.

At the Guangzhou Auto Show this week, Li Auto’s rival XPeng (XPEV) outlined its expansion plans outside China. The company now plans five new overseas models in 2027, and aims to more than double overseas sales next year after topping 100,000 this year, and targets international robotaxi and IRON humanoid-robot deployments later in 2027.
NIO’s (NIO) more affordable Firefly brand, meanwhile, reached 100,000 cumulative deliveries about 19 months after its start and expects November volume to exceed 10,000 for the first time.

All the stocks clocked considerable gains this week. Overall, TSLA clocked 16% gains, marking its best week since May 2025. RIVN clocked 18% gains, marking its best week since July, while LI clocked its best week since September 2024 with 20% gains, while NIO added 15% and XPEV 16%. LCID was the sole player to clock single-digit gains.

title: Zero To Sixty: Tesla Cybercab Fleet Tops 1,000 In Texas, Lucid Starts Fully Driverless Tests And Chinese EV Maker Posts Stronger Margins
